claims.text: Replacing laser powder bed fusion with binder jet printing followed by low-temperature sintering will reduce residual thermal stresses in AlCrFeNiSi miniature components.
Binder jet printing followed by low-temperature sintering will preserve or improve the mechanical properties of AlCrFeNiSi miniature components.
The proposed process change will simplify processing relative to high-thermal-load laser-based additive manufacturing.
The feedstock is pre-alloyed AlCrFeNiSi powder with spherical morphology.
Binder jet printing is to be performed through binder deposition at room temperature.
The printed components are to be sintered in a protective atmosphere below the material's melting point.
Binder jet printing and subsequent sintering impose lower thermal gradients than laser-based melting.
Lower thermal gradients limit residual-stress development.
The reduced thermal load of binder jet printing minimizes rapid thermal cycling relative to laser-based melting.
Moderating rapid thermal cycling and thermal gradients limits the accumulation of residual stress and deleterious microstructural changes.
Controlled low-temperature sintering can densify AlCrFeNiSi components without exposing them to high thermal shock.
Binder-jet-printed and sintered components will have lower residual stress than otherwise identical laser-powder-bed-fused components.
Binder-jet-printed and sintered components will retain or improve yield strength and toughness relative to laser-powder-bed-fused components.
The hypothesis applies only to miniature geometries and processing windows in which sintering can reliably densify AlCrFeNiSi without introducing additional defects.
